rationale: Round 5, lens: AC falsifiability and internal consistency, re-read from disk at 7404845f. All 6 of my round-4 asks are ADDRESSED (round-ordered F2 with equal-or-ancestor anchors and the exits named in both reattest's refusal and MF-3 arm 1b; lazy plan.md read with checkout-then-spec/<S>-then-all-N4 and AC-4 (iv) pinned at zero reads; O/X/H titles pinned to the full spec ID; AC-3 gains both N4-positional legs with exact red-on-revert; AC-11 (x) is written out as a topology; the staged ms-bead-impl line carries an inline target+remove-by marker that AC-18 pins). On the attack the BRIEF asked for: a later UNLANDED round's SHA cannot be an anchor on a legitimate registration set — an ancestor of the candidate's second parent is an ancestor of the merge, which the fallback admits only when reachable from the tip, so such a SHA is landed by definition and cannot be the non-ancestor that triggers F2; the only way a later round becomes an anchor is a forged or mis-written registration, which is panel.json (agent-writable, ADR-0037 §8), and the spec's residual paragraph should say so because it currently presents 'the panel scan' as a trustworthy input next to 'metadata'. I verified the mechanics the rule rests on: this panel's own panel.json reads round 5 bumped in place, 48 registrations in the repo carry round ≥ 2 versus 12 at round 1, no `-r2` dirs exist, and the ms-panel-run skill co-bumps round and reviewed_head_sha on `--round N+1`; under that single-dir convention O3's shape leaves only {round k: B} with no anchor, which F2 fails closed on, and the rebased-away round vanishes, so the legitimate case passes. What remains are four minors, all pins: the residual statement and an optional git-derived anchor tightening; an AC-11 leg for the single-registration no-anchor shape (the real-world O3 shape, which (vii)–(x-t) do not exercise); AC-1's Q row depends on which duplicate epic the title fallback picks and N2a's 'parent is a bead P' needs 'non-epic'; and OQ-9's 'member set equals what GateReadiness can pass' needs the plan-source caveat R1.1 itself states. None is a contradiction that would make an AC unfalsifiable, so I approve with asks.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 residual / ADR-0041 (i): state that F2's inputs are panel registrations (panel.json files and their `round` fields), which are agent-writable like the binding, so a forged registration with a high `round` whose reviewed_head_sha is ANY ancestor of the candidate's second parent (e.g. the spec-branch base) raises the highest anchor round and neutralises F2 for a later unlanded review; a legitimate registration set cannot do this (a later round that is an ancestor of the second parent is landed by construction). Optional, cheap hardening to pin if adopted: an anchor's SHA must be reachable from the second parent AND NOT reachable from the merge's first parent (it must lie on the bead side), which excludes the spec-base trick without touching #233's shape; add the corresponding AC-11 leg (forged high-round anchor at the spec base → still refuses).

AC-11: add the single-registration shape that the in-place round bump actually produces — O3's attack with ONE registration dir `{round 2: B}` (A's round overwritten): MF-3 FAILS naming the candidate and reattest REFUSES because a non-ancestor exists with no anchor (F2's 'no anchor' branch has no leg today; (x-t) covers only ties and missing rounds). Pair it with the legitimate single-dir #239 shape `{round 2: B}` where B is the second parent or its ancestor → accepted, so both branches of the common convention are pinned.

AC-1: (a) row Q relies on `FindEpicForBead`'s title fallback choosing the duplicate epic E′ over E; Background K says the newest epic wins nondeterministically across lookups, so pin the fixture (E′ created after E, and the fake epic list ordered accordingly) or Q's expected class is not reproducible; (b) R1.2 N2a reads 'the row's parent is a bead P the agent did not name' — define P as a NON-EPIC bead, otherwise the conditional `parent: E2` variant of row X matches N2a (first in the classification order) instead of N2c.

OQ-9 'What this gives: the member set equals the beads that GateReadiness can pass on MF-1 and lineage' — qualify with R1.1 (c)'s own caveat: selection may read plan.md from `spec/<S>` while `EvaluateReadiness` reads the invoking checkout, so from a checkout without plan.md a member can be selected and then refused by readiness's 'reading plan.md' error. Either make readiness read the same source (plan decision) or state the equality holds only when both read the same file.

findings.title: Anchor/round rule attack: a later unlanded round cannot legitimately be an anchor; the round mechanics the rule assumes are real
findings.detail: Let M be the admitted fallback candidate (reachable from the spec tip by construction) with second parent P2. A registration SHA R that equals or is an ancestor of P2 is an ancestor of M and therefore of the tip, so R is landed and can never be the 'not an ancestor of the spec tip' registration F2 refuses on; conversely an unlanded R cannot be an ancestor of P2. So on a truthful registration set, anchors are exactly the landed reviews and the equal-or-ancestor widening only admits #233's tree-identical complete commit. The widening does NOT admit a later unlanded round. Mechanics verified: this panel's panel.json is `round: 5` with the current SHA (bumped in place); across the repo 48 panel.json files carry round ≥ 2 and 12 carry round 1; no `-r2` directories exist; plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-panel-run/SKILL.md documents `--round N+1` co-bumping round and reviewed_head_sha in one write. Under that single-dir convention O3's shape leaves `{round 2: B}` with no anchor (A overwritten) → fail closed → refuse, and a rebased-away earlier round is overwritten → `{round 2: B}` anchors → pass; both outcomes are what the spec intends, but only the two-dir fixtures are pinned (see the AC-11 ask). The equal-only alternative would indeed fail closed on every complete-landed bead (B ≠ D), so the reviser's argument holds.

findings.title: The residual omits that F2's anchors come from agent-writable panel.json, and a forged high-round anchor defeats F2
findings.detail: R4.2 says F1–F5 run 'from git and the panel scan, never from metadata' and that a metadata forge 'can make MF-3 accept only a candidate that reattest itself would accept'. Registrations are files an agent can write (ADR-0037 §8 already accepts panel.json forgery as the defended boundary). A registration dir with `round: 99` and reviewed_head_sha = the spec-branch base (an ancestor of every bead's second parent) makes the highest anchor round 99, so a genuinely later unlanded review (round 2) no longer refuses; reattest then accepts O3's shape and the read-back passes F2 forever. This is inside the accepted class, but the residual text should name it rather than imply the panel scan is more trustworthy than bd metadata. A git-derived tightening — anchor SHA reachable from P2 and not from M's first parent — removes the base-commit trick at no cost to #233.

findings.title: AC-11 has no leg for F2's 'no anchor while a non-ancestor exists' branch, which is the real-world O3 shape
findings.detail: (vii), (viii), (ix), (ix-f) all register two dirs `{round 1: A, round 2: B}`; (x-t) covers a tie and a missing round. With the in-place bump that ms-panel-run performs, the attack leaves a single registration `{round 2: B}` and no anchor at all; the spec says this fails closed, but no AC exercises that branch, and nothing pins that the legitimate single-dir `{round k: B}` (B = P2 or its ancestor) is accepted.

findings.title: AC-1 row Q's class is not reproducible as written, and N2a's 'bead P' admits an epic
findings.detail: Q (`<E>.6`, no parent, title `[S] …`) is expected to resolve by the title fallback to a duplicate epic E′ with the same spec number. FindEpicForBeadWithCache iterates c.AllEpics() and Background K says the newest epic wins nondeterministically; the fixture must fix the order (E′ newer, or the fake's epic list ordered E′ first), otherwise Q is a member in one run and N2b in another. Separately, R1.2 N2a is 'the row's parent is a bead P the agent did not name' and comes first in the classification order; the conditional X variant uses `parent: E2` (an epic), which would then match N2a rather than the intended N2c unless P is defined as a non-epic bead.

findings.title: OQ-9's equality claim is wider than R1.1 (c)'s plan-source caveat allows
findings.detail: OQ-9: 'The member set equals the beads that GateReadiness can pass on MF-1 and lineage, for <E>.<N> IDs.' R1.1 (c): selection falls back to `git show spec/<S>:…/plan.md` while `EvaluateReadiness` reads only the checkout's file, and 'Selection can then name a member that GateReadiness refuses with readiness's existing reading-plan.md error'. The two sentences disagree for a checkout without plan.md; one should yield.
